stories.title: ESMA backs limited taxonomy opex disclosures
stories.summary: Europe's markets regulator ESMA supports limited taxonomy opex disclosures, Responsible Investor reports in its news round-up. The same briefing covers Nest's first paper on social investment factors and a COP31 AI pledge seeking investor signatories. The full items are behind a paywall.

stories.title: Ukraine sets a 2027 to 2030 plan for EU-style sustainability reporting
stories.summary: Ukraine's Cabinet of Ministers has approved an action plan for 2027 to 2030 to keep bringing corporate sustainability reporting in line with EU standards, the Finance Ministry said. It sets tasks, deadlines and owners, continuing a strategy approved in October 2024.

stories.title: Tunisia's market regulator publishes its sustainability strategy
stories.summary: Tunisia's Financial Market Council has published a report on its priorities for sustainable finance. It describes how the regulator is gradually bringing ESG considerations into the practices of market participants and raising companies' awareness of sustainability reporting.

stories.title: Green capabilities only pay where the systems around them exist
stories.summary: In an ESG News essay, Professor Ioannis Ioannou argues that firms and governments must build infrastructure, markets and rules together. He cites ArcelorMittal dropping hydrogen steel plans in Germany in 2025 despite 1.3 billion euros of public money, and Renewcell's 2024 bankruptcy.

stories.title: SeABank splits its sustainable finance framework three ways
stories.summary: Vietnam's SeABank expects to allocate 40 to 45% of its new framework to green projects, 10 to 15% to blue and 40 to 45% to social. S&P Global Ratings gave a second-party opinion, and projects must show at least a 20% improvement in energy, emissions or water use.

stories.title: Indian miners say ESG norms add to an already hard funding problem
stories.summary: At ET Infra's Global Metals and Mining Meet, speakers said mining already needs heavy financial engineering because of commodity prices, site feasibility and long timelines. Resurgent India's Jyoti Prakash Gadia said ESG compliance norms have added a new challenge for raising money.

stories.title: Safaricom maps its business against nine SDGs
stories.summary: Safaricom's 2026 Sustainable Business report focuses on nine UN development goals it considers most relevant, from health and education to clean energy and partnerships. It uses the Alexforbes Paragon SDG Impact Assessment to weigh positive and negative effects of its activities.

stories.title: Brabners hires a social impact manager after B Corp re-certification
stories.summary: UK law firm Brabners has appointed Freya Grummitt to a newly created Social Impact Manager role following its B Corp re-certification. She brings 15 years of experience in responsible business and social impact work across consultancy, public sector and corporate roles.

stories.title: Flint Group Packaging Solutions announces its 2025 sustainability report
stories.summary: Flint Group Packaging Solutions will publish its full year 2025 sustainability report under its PRISM framework, covering environment, people and governance. The announcement highlights that the company kept its EcoVadis Gold rating for the second consecutive year.

stories.title: A primer on telling ESG claims from greenwashing
stories.summary: Dynamite News walks consumers through the environmental, social and governance pillars to help separate real action from misleading claims. It says companies making genuine environmental progress should back claims with measurable targets and transparent performance reports.

stories.title: Sustainability report finalists on making reports people actually read
stories.summary: BusinessGreen speaks to finalists in the UK Green Business Awards' Sustainability Report of the Year category about balancing eye-catching design with credibility. The full article was blocked to us, so only the teaser was available.

stories.title: CEOs say AI has not yet transformed their businesses
stories.summary: CEOs say they are not yet seeing transformational change from AI, ESG Dive reports, though more than six in ten US leaders told KPMG their firms were moving at the right pace or ahead. Only the teaser was available to us.

stories.title: Lynas reports 93% renewable power in its FY26 sustainability report
stories.summary: Lynas Rare Earths has released its FY26 sustainability report, citing revenue of $977.9 million and 93% renewable power output, according to a Kalkine headline. The article was blocked to us, so only the headline was available.

stories.title: Jharkhand picks five government schemes to earn carbon credits
stories.summary: Jharkhand's forest and climate department held a workshop on turning five existing government programmes into carbon credit projects. State nodal officer Ravi Ranjan said the aim is to monetise carbon-reduction work and bring extra income to rural communities.

stories.title: CMPDIL and QCI-NABET hold a carbon credits workshop for coal
stories.summary: Central Mine Planning and Design Institute and QCI-NABET held a workshop in Ranchi on ESG and carbon credits for the coal sector. It followed their September 18 agreement and covered greenhouse gas accounting, offset markets and energy efficiency for mining.

stories.title: Jain Irrigation signs a biochar credit deal for up to 19,000 tonnes
stories.summary: Jain Irrigation has agreed to supply London marketplace Supercritical with up to 19,000 tonnes of biochar carbon removal credits. The credits will come from gasifying agricultural residues at its Jalgaon facility in 2026 and 2027.

stories.title: India says it needs $220 billion for its 2030 clean power goal
stories.summary: India's government estimates it needs about $220 billion between 2027 and 2030 to reach 500 GW of non-fossil power capacity. The money would go to solar, wind, transmission, storage, green hydrogen and manufacturing, with more private and foreign investment sought.

stories.title: Panama consolidates a national carbon market roadmap
stories.summary: Panama has pulled years of technical work, private sector engagement and public dialogue into one roadmap for carbon markets. Its environment ministry has worked on the groundwork since 2017, and carbon market cooperation is on the agenda at COP31 in Turkiye.

stories.title: Argentina's Senate passes a carbon market bill 60 to 2
stories.summary: Argentina's Senate approved a national carbon market framework by 60 votes to two, sending it to the Chamber of Deputies. Industry estimates put potential carbon credit exports at up to $3.9 billion a year, while environmental groups have raised oversight concerns.

stories.title: The Philippines names its carbon market authority
stories.summary: Executive Order 127, signed on October 13, makes the Philippines' environment department the national authority for carbon markets, a Manila Times editorial notes. It argues the new framework must settle whether benefits are real, who owns them and whether reductions get counted twice.

stories.title: Sindh approves 13 carbon market projects
stories.summary: Sindh has approved 13 carbon market projects it says could cut 330.13 million tonnes of emissions, environment secretary Faisal Ahmed Uqaili said at a workshop held ahead of COP31. The province has also prepared six priority climate projects worth $62.15 million.

stories.title: UN expert warns carbon markets may undermine climate action
stories.summary: A report by UN Special Rapporteur Elisa Morgera says research, court decisions and community experience show carbon markets encourage low-quality credits, over-crediting and greenwashing. She called for an urgent reassessment and said reliance on credits may clash with human rights obligations.

stories.title: Australia's carbon credit reforms draw fire from both sides
stories.summary: An inquiry has heard that changes to Australia's carbon credit scheme would send chills through the market. Academics and environmental groups said the reforms do not go far enough, likening some revegetation projects to regrowing forests on the moon. Only a short excerpt was available.

stories.title: Verra releases combined templates for carbon and co-benefits
stories.summary: Verra has released eight combined templates for projects certified under both its Verified Carbon Standard and its Climate, Community and Biodiversity Standards. It has also moved the effective date for VCS Version 5 from January 1 to July 1, 2027.

stories.title: What happens to carbon credits when the forest burns
stories.summary: CNA Explains looks at Indonesia's wildfires reaching areas linked to forest carbon projects whose credits are bought by companies, including some in Singapore. It asks whether the credits still count, who bears the cost of the released carbon and whether safeguards are strong enough.

stories.title: TPG closes two climate funds at $10.4 billion
stories.summary: TPG held a final close on Rise Climate II and its Global South Initiative with $10.4 billion in commitments. The Global South fund, launched at COP28, hit its $2.5 billion target, and investors new to TPG supplied 31% of the money.

stories.title: BRAC Bank plans Bangladesh's first Tk 1,000 crore green bond
stories.summary: BRAC Bank will issue a three-year zero-coupon green bond of Tk 1,000 crore, the first aligned with Bangladesh Bank's green bond policy. Proceeds go to renewable energy, green buildings and industrial energy efficiency, with each bond priced at Tk 10 lakh.

stories.title: COP17 ends with a review saying nature targets will be missed
stories.summary: Countries at the COP17 biodiversity talks in Yerevan completed the first global review of progress, which warns the 2030 goal of reversing nature loss will not be met unless action is rapidly accelerated. Non-donor countries can now signal interest in contributing finance before COP18.

stories.title: COP17 invites China and Gulf states to help fund nature
stories.summary: Governments at COP17 in Armenia agreed to scale up biodiversity policies and, for the first time, invited large emerging economies such as China and Gulf states to take on donor roles. A UN report found the world off track on 22 of 23 targets.

stories.title: Calls grow to reform the UN biodiversity summits
stories.summary: With governments on track to keep their record of never meeting a target in the convention's 34-year history, calls for reform of UN biodiversity summits are growing, the Guardian reports. COP17 closed with countries vowing to redouble efforts on the 2030 goals.

stories.title: EU rules out new climate finance pledges at COP31
stories.summary: EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra said the bloc will make no new climate finance commitments at COP31, calling further emissions funding dead in the water, according to Bloomberg. African nations plan to demand a tripling of adaptation finance at the summit.

stories.title: Canada says it is finding solutions on the EU carbon border levy
stories.summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney said there are common solutions to the EU's carbon import levy on Canadian iron ore, steel, aluminium and cement. Canada's ambassador said the EU will recognise Canada's carbon price. CBAM ramps up to full implementation in 2034.

stories.title: UK consults on extending its carbon border levy to fuels
stories.summary: The UK has opened a consultation on extending its Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism to petrol, diesel and jet fuel, with responses due January 20, 2027. The existing UK CBAM starts on January 1, 2027, covering aluminium, cement, fertiliser, hydrogen, iron and steel.

stories.title: Europe's steel border now has two locks
stories.summary: Fastmarkets says the EU's carbon border levy and its new tariff-rate quotas together mean a carbon-competitive overseas mill can still be shut out. It forecasts green steel imports rising from 0.3 million to 1.6 million tonnes over the decade.

stories.title: CEEW says the UNFCCC should take up carbon border taxes
stories.summary: A CEEW paper notes that after the EU's CBAM, the UK plans a similar levy in 2027 and others are considering one. It argues the cross-border effects on trade and market access are especially significant for developing countries and calls for cooperation through the UNFCCC.

stories.title: India's non-fossil capacity passes 300 GW ahead of COP31
stories.summary: India's non-fossil power capacity reached 300.5 GW in July 2026 after a record 55.29 GW was added in FY2025-26, including 44.6 GW of solar. Assocham says the next phase needs more focus on grids, storage and commercially viable clean power.

stories.title: Nepal and Bhutan seek a mountain agenda at COP31
stories.summary: Nepal and Bhutan have jointly proposed a dedicated agenda item on 1.5 degree warming in mountain regions for COP31, scheduled for November 9 to 20 in Antalya. Nepal's environment minister Geeta Chaudhary submitted the proposal.

stories.title: Tanzania sets out its COP31 priorities
stories.summary: Tanzania will push for better access to climate finance, adaptation, technology transfer and ecosystem restoration at COP31 in Antalya. It is also targeting clean cooking access for 80% of its population by 2034.

stories.title: How a 2005 UN vote shaped the carbon capture debate
stories.summary: A ProPublica and Drilled investigation, republished by Asia Times, revisits the 2005 UN scientists' meeting in Oviedo, Spain, that finished a landmark report on carbon capture and storage. Hosts handed out cava labelled for those who truly believed the barely tested technology could work.

stories.title: Which Indian packaging can actually be recycled
stories.summary: The Indian Express looks at milk packets, chip wrappers and paper bags and what India's waste system can realistically recycle. EcoEx chief executive Akshaya Rath says technology can help producers and brand owners with extended producer responsibility compliance and traceability.

stories.title: Jammu and Kashmir sets up a four-tier circular economy mechanism
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir has created a UT-level Circular Economy Mission, a steering committee, district cells and urban local body committees to implement its Circular Economy Policy 2026. The mission is headed by the Chief Secretary, according to the Daily Excelsior.

stories.title: EPL on recyclable tubes and recycled plastic
stories.summary: Packaging maker EPL's Hariharan K. Nair tells The CSR Universe the challenge is making packaging recyclable without hurting protection, function or cost. EPL is developing recyclable tube formats and using more post-consumer recycled material through platforms such as Platina.

stories.title: Jordan approves a circular economy roadmap to 2050
stories.summary: Jordan's Cabinet has endorsed a National Circular Economy Roadmap through 2050, written by the environment and industry ministries with the Royal Scientific Society. It aims to rethink how the country uses energy, water and raw materials, the Petra news agency reports.

stories.title: Quang Ninh pilots burning household waste in cement kilns
stories.summary: A Norway-funded UNDP project launched in Vietnam's Quang Ninh on October 30 combines waste sorting at source, recovery of recyclables and co-processing of household waste in cement kilns. The aim is to send less waste to landfill and build a model for replication.

stories.title: Korean ESG adviser pitches renting products instead of selling them
stories.summary: Kim Jae-hong of the Korean ESG Society told a Ho Chi Minh City forum that companies should keep ownership of products and charge usage fees. He argued this product-as-a-service model can raise profits and supply chain stability while moving beyond recycling.

stories.title: Biobased plastics need a full circular accounting
stories.summary: Innovation News Network argues that swapping fossil carbon for plant carbon solves only half the problem. The material must perform, but its production and recovery must also improve the wider system, which depends on factories, collection and the land supplying biomass.

stories.title: Mondragon shows its circular economy work at Circular Week 2026
stories.summary: Cooperative group Mondragon held a session at Circular Week 2026 on how industrial ecosystems can drive the circular economy at scale. Professionals from several of its cooperatives presented solutions for more circular production and consumption.

stories.title: ENGIE commissions 200 MW of solar at Khavda
stories.summary: ENGIE has commissioned a 200 MW solar project in the Khavda Renewable Energy Park in Gujarat's Kutch district, part of 450 MW it has brought online in India. The plant should generate about 350 million units a year for Gujarat Urja Vikas Nigam.

stories.title: NTPC Green Energy's quarterly profit rises 57%
stories.summary: NTPC Green Energy reported a 57% rise in standalone net profit to Rs 137.5 crore for the second quarter of FY2026-27, up from Rs 86.04 crore a year earlier. Revenue rose 53%.

stories.title: Vikram Solar wins a 289.87 MWp module order from NLC India
stories.summary: Vikram Solar will supply 289.87 MWp of N-type TOPCon modules to NLC India Renewables for an 810 MW solar project at the RUVN Solar Park in Pugal, Bikaner. NLC India Renewables is a wholly owned NLC subsidiary.

stories.title: Solid Solar builds a 20 MWp plant on a single hill
stories.summary: Solid Solar has commissioned a roughly 20 MWp solar project in Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, built on one hill more than 5,000 feet above sea level. It calls it one of India's largest hilly-terrain solar plants, using Gautam Solar's bifacial modules.

stories.title: Power Grid wants cable makers to ramp up
stories.summary: Power Grid Corporation of India expects capital spending to exceed last year's Rs 40,000 crore as it builds transmission for renewables, urbanisation and data centres. It is asking cable and wire makers to raise production to keep pace, Livemint reports.

stories.title: Report calls green hydrogen an industrial strategy question for India
stories.summary: A CareEdge report says green hydrogen is not India's whole decarbonisation plan but is central to its industrial competitiveness. It cites EU carbon border exposure, the 2070 net zero goal, cheap renewables and funded policy as conditions few emerging economies can match.

stories.title: Microsoft's cloud boom raises its energy question
stories.summary: Microsoft reported first quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19%, with Microsoft Cloud revenue up 30% to $63.9 billion, CarbonCredits.com reports. The piece says the AI infrastructure behind that growth brings a major sustainability challenge.

stories.title: Sasol's 2030 emissions target looks increasingly back-loaded
stories.summary: Investor group Just Share says Sasol's emissions rose this year and will keep rising as production grows, leaving heavy cuts needed to hit its 30% target by 2030. Shareholders have not been invited to vote on its climate plans.

stories.title: Investors cautiously welcome BP's concessions
stories.summary: Responsible Investor reports that BP has acknowledged shareholder concerns after a bruising AGM and investors are waiting to see the concessions turn into action. The full article sits behind a registration wall, so only the opening was available to us.

stories.title: Shell, BP and Equinor report bumper third quarter profits
stories.summary: BusinessGreen reports that the Middle East crisis helped Shell, BP and Equinor more than double year-on-year profits, which campaigners called a kick in the teeth for UK billpayers. Only the teaser was available to us.

stories.title: Meta signs a low-carbon cement deal with Fortera
stories.summary: Meta's deal with Fortera gives it the equivalent of 200,000 tons of environmental attribute credits plus access to low-carbon cement for its own projects, ESG Dive reports. Only the teaser was available to us.

stories.title: The Senedd joins Cardiff's low-carbon heat network
stories.summary: The Senedd, Ty Hywel and the Wales Millennium Centre have connected to Cardiff's low-carbon heat network, removing the need for gas boilers, according to BusinessGreen. The full article was blocked to us, so only the teaser was available.

stories.title: UK heat pump grants hit a monthly record in September
stories.summary: September brought the highest number of grants ever issued in one month under the UK's Boiler Upgrade Scheme, according to figures reported by BusinessGreen. Only the teaser was available to us, so the exact count is not given here.

research.title: NASA telescope on verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
research.summary: Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission's chief scientist

research.title: On umbrellas, springs, and superconductivity
research.summary: Springs are usually metal wires wound in a spiral, allowing us to store mechanical energy, the umbrella’s rod consists of multiple cylinders, and the spring opens them up in succession, when you close an umbrella, you compress the spring and store energy in it

research.title: Scientists unearth new instance of ‘contagious cancer’ in animals
research.summary: Researchers studied melanoma in the brown bullhead catfish, a resident of Lake Memphremagog, between Quebec in Canada and Vermont in the U.S., the finding is interesting because it could reveal clues to keeping a human’s body from rejecting a transplanted organ

research.title: To overcome technical hurdles, ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan
research.summary: Pyro valves are crucial in spacecraft propulsion, and it may be recalled that the NVS-02 (launched in 2025), the second spacecraft in the NVS series, was a failure. To overcome technical hurdles, ISRO flew NVS-03 satellite with pyro valves open: Narayanan

research.title: AI can help experts tell a real Rembrandt from a fake
research.summary: A newly developed AI model aids art attribution, which traditionally takes a trained human eye and several tools, reports a new research paper. AI can help experts tell a real Rembrandt from a fake

research.title: Nearly 20% of Switzerland’s glacier ice has vanished in just five years
research.summary: Switzerland’s glaciers are disappearing at an alarming rate, losing more than 5% of their ice volume in 2026 alone. Some of the country’s most famous glaciers experienced their worst melting on record, while several smaller glaciers vanished completely. Nearly 20% of Switzerland’s glacier ice has disappeared in just.

research.title: One of Earth’s most powerful supervolcanoes is refilling with fresh magma
research.summary: Deep beneath Japan’s Kikai caldera, a massive magma reservoir is refilling 7,300 years after one of the most powerful volcanic eruptions in Earth's recent geological history. Scientists used underwater seismic surveys to reveal a vast store of magma that appears to have accumulated since the ancient catastrophe. The.

research.title: A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea and unleashed a 330-foot tsunami
research.summary: A decades-long mystery beneath the North Sea has finally been solved. Scientists have confirmed that the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was created when a 160-meter-wide asteroid struck Earth roughly 43 to 46 million years ago. The violent collision blasted a towering curtain of rock.
